Sen. Gallego Sees ‘Good Grounds’ for Hegseth Impeachment
videos.description: Arizona Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego, a Marine Corps combat veteran who served in Iraq, says what he describes as efforts to sidestep Congress on war powers provide “good grounds” for Pete Hegseth’s impeachment, while saying he would review the evidence before any Senate trial. Sen. Gallego also calls for scrutiny of whether outside influence played a role in Nvidia’s push to loosen chip export controls on China, and says the crypto industry will have to talk to returning Sen. Sherrod Brown and “ask for some forgiveness” after spending heavily against him. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Capitol Hill on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." -------- More on Bloomberg Television and Markets Like this video? videos.title: Rep. LaLota ‘Bullish’ on Bipartisan Lame-Duck Deals
videos.description: New York Republican Congressman Nick LaLota reacts to Jim Jordan’s election as incoming House minority leader, while praising Steve Scalise’s record and political skills. Rep. LaLota says he’s confident Republicans can work with Democrats on affordability and other shared priorities, and says he’s “bullish” Congress can use the lame-duck session to make progress on government funding and other bipartisan legislation. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Capitol Hill on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." -------- More on Bloomberg Television and Markets Like this video? videos.title: Jensen Huang’s 700,000% Return Magnifies Nvidia Succession Risks
videos.description: The office of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang has an unusual setup: The chief executive officer sits at an enormous oval desk facing his lieutenants, with room for more employees in stadium seating behind them. The arrangement — created as part of Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California — is purpose-built to suit how Huang runs the company. Though it’s not uncommon to see cultlike tech CEOs who obsess over details, Huang is in a class of his own. He has led the business since its very beginning 33 years ago, the longest such run in Silicon Valley. And even as Nvidia grew into one of the world’s most powerful companies — with a stock return of more than 700,000% — there’s still no one designated to potentially replace him.
